title: Hybrid budget throttler and GPU-preference routing policy for multi-tier inference
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Implement a hybrid budget throttler and GPU-preference routing policy that enforces hierarchical spend caps (global -> org -> route) while optimizing for unit cost using spot/on-demand signals and GPU affinity scores. The system should provide soft throttles (graceful degradation) and hard caps, support model-variant fallback (e.g., full fp16 -> q4_0 family -> distilled variant), and expose per-tenant spend windows and real-time cost telemetry for the Console. The implementation must respect latency SLOs by applying progressive degradation policies and preferring GPU types that minimize expected per-token cost subject to SLO constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Hierarchical caps enforceable: global, org, route with configurable soft/hard thresholds
Routing decision includes GPU-affinity score and spot-price signal to pick cheapest compatible node while meeting latency SLO
Progressive fallback chain for model variants implemented and exercised in e2e tests
Console shows per-tenant spend projection, remaining budget, and live routed vs fallback counts
No regression in P50/P95 latency for premium routes (verified on staging)
comments: 2025-02-12 Maya Thompson: RFC created linking spend-smoothing window idea and penalty curves; initial design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Hybrid+Budget+Throttler+RFC

2025-02-19 Arjun Patel: Spike complete - collected spot price variance telemetry across regions. Found us-east-1 spot churn spikes ~18% weekly for our DL instances. Implication: aggressive spot-skimming needs a fallback runway to avoid SLO violations.

2025-02-20 Lina Moreno (PM): Prefer soft-throttle default for PLG orgs to avoid sudden customer errors; enterprise orgs should be allowed hard caps via contract. Added label request for per-org config UI.

2025-02-25 Evan Cho (Design): Reviewed Console mocks. Request: surface projected spend and estimated degradation impact (example: expected latency increase when falling back to q4 family). Link to mock: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1X-example

2025-02-27 Arjun Patel: Prototype routing algorithm implemented in routing-service branch; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5621. Early tests show 12% token-cost reduction for batch-y workloads at 5% SLO budget impact when spot capacity available.

2025-03-01 Reliability review (Priya Singh): Raised concern about race conditions when applying hard caps during autoscaler events. Proposed mitigation: central cap coordinator with idempotent apply & lease-based enforcement.
2025-03-03 Maya Thompson: Added dependency on ENG-21904 for region-capacity awareness and ENG-31245 for budgeted fallback metrics. Planning to run canary in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 first.

2025-03-04 Arjun Patel: Updated implementation plan to include a canary rollout and abort criteria: abort if error rate increases > 2x baseline or P95 latency regresses > 30% for premium routes. Updated staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/routing-costs
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Unit + integration tests (routing-service + autoscaler) -> Phase 2: Staging canary in us-west-2 (5% traffic) with Console visibility -> Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% & split across tiers -> Phase 4: Global rollout with per-org defaults and opt-outs. Abort conditions and metrics documented in RFC.
implementation_notes: Key pieces: cap coordinator (leases), GPU-affinity score engine, spot-price feed adapter, fallback chain registry, Console UI for cap configs. Trade-offs: tighter spot-skimming increases cost savings but requires more robust fallback runway. Decided to implement configurable penalty curves to smooth spend and avoid cliffing.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring and cap enforcement, integration tests with autoscaler simulator, chaos tests that kill spot nodes to validate fallback, e2e billing simulation to validate reconciliation with accounting service.
operational_runbook: Runbook draft in Confluence. Include steps: how to temporarily lift soft caps for an org, how to drain canary region, how to disable GPU-preference scoring if it causes regressions. Pager escalation to SRE if canary abort criteria triggered.
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus review on: lease semantics for cap coordinator, idempotency guarantees, and proposed metric set for Console (projected_spend, remaining_budget_pct, routed_count, fallback_count, avg_unit_cost). PM Lina will review UX changes separately.
